title: Query Gateway Permission Shaper — adaptive view-level RBAC for analytics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We will implement a Permission Shaper component in the Query Gateway that materializes per-request view-level permissions for analytics endpoints and usage dashboards. The shaper computes the allowed projection (columns), row filters (tenant/organization scoping), and capability flags (export/csv/download) and attaches a short-lived signed permission token to downstream queries and pipeline requests.

Goals:
- Centralize enforcement of view-level RBAC so all analytics endpoints (per-route usage views, timeseries, export APIs) use the same contract.
- Keep per-request latency impact < 6ms p50 for common cached scenarios and < 15ms p95 for cold evals.
- Provide audit-ready traces for permission decisions and an ability to revoke tokens (TTL + revocation list).
- Integrate with existing entitlement syncer and analytics-permission-cache subsystems.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Permission model: We will support three evaluation modes: cached token (fast path), delta-token (small patch for minor roles), and full-eval (authorization service call). Cached token will be derived from entitlement snapshot + role-hash and stored in the Permission Cache with a 10m TTL. Full-eval is required for changes with high-sensitivity labels or immediate admin revocation.
- Enforcement point: Query Gateway inspects token and injects the computed row filters into SQL/Elastic queries as a parameterized WHERE clause. For legacy pipelines that cannot accept injected filters, the gateway will fall back to an enforced pre-filter stage in the projection service.
- Performance vs correctness: We accept occasional stale-cached decisions for up to 10m to keep P95 latency tight; for customers selecting strict audit mode, we support immediate full-eval by setting request header X-Auth-Aggressiveness=strict which forces fresh evaluation and is logged as high-cost.
- Security: Tokens are HMAC-signed with key rotation managed by KMS. Token includes minimal claims: principal_id, view_id, role_hash, allowed_columns (hash), row_filter_version, exp. We avoid serializing raw predicates in tokens to reduce token size.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spike (done): micro-prototype of permission token encoding + cache eviction semantics. Perf baseline and memory budget documented in Confluence.
2) Core shaper service (week 1-2): implement permission evaluation library + deterministic column projection generator. Expose GRPC and HTTP endpoints for Query Gateway.
3) Query Gateway integration (week 3): token validation, WHERE injection, and fallback flow. Add feature flag gate: feature.analytics_permission_shaper.
4) Cache & entitlements sync (week 3-4): integrate with entitlement-syncer and permission-cache (depends on ENG-35741).
5) Tests & E2E (week 4): property tests for projection correctness, RBAC regression harness using existing eval prompt sets, perf tests.
6) Gradual rollout (week 5): canary in us-east on 10% traffic, monitor errors and latency, then ramp.

Telemetry & observability:
- Emit permission_decision events with reason, cache_hit boolean, evaluation_mode, and latency_ms.
- Add a dashboard in Console (link below) tracking cache hit rate, avg eval latency, error rate, and top failing predicates.
- Hook into Console rollout traces so SRE can correlate permission rejections with downstream query failures.

Security & compliance:
- Security review required (ticket flagged). We will deliver threat model and KMS rotation plan to Security.
- Audit log lines for each decision will be exported to the existing analytics-audit-sink for 90 days.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Query+Gateway+Permission+Shaper
- Design diagram & sequence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Permission+Shaper+Sequence+Diagrams
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3456 (permission-token prototype)

Open questions / risks:
- Query injection safe-lists: we need a catalog of allowed SQL constructs per view to avoid injection when injecting row filters. Engineering to produce a whitelist by 2026-02-05.
- Cost of revocation: if we attempt immediate revocation we may need to force pipeline cache invalidation—trade-off between immediacy and throughput.
- Backwards compatibility: some legacy export jobs assume full-table reads; we will add transformation helpers but may need opt-in migration.

Next immediate steps:
- Finish API spec for shaper library and finalize token schema (owner: Ravi Patel) by 2026-01-25.
- Security review kickoff with Security team on 2026-01-28.
- Spike integration with query-builder library to validate WHERE injection approach (owner: Priya Kapoor).
comments: 2026-01-20 - Spike complete: permission token prototype implemented, cache semantics validated. Perf baseline: cached token validation ~1.8ms p50; full-eval ~9ms p50 on staging infra.
2026-01-28 - Design review with Security and Data Platform. Security requested threat model doc and KMS key rotation plan. Action: schedule secure design walkthrough.
2026-02-11 - Prototype PR #3456 reviewed by @liam.oconnor. Feedback: tighten token claim set and add explicit audit_reason field. Action assigned to Ravi.
2026-02-21 - Integrated permission cache with entitlement-syncer on dev. Observed cache churn for orgs with frequent role updates; plan to group updates into 30s batches.
2026-03-05 - Query Gateway injection prototype validated with Timeseries and Export endpoints. Found one legacy export job that expects raw CSV access; created migration ticket ENG-52690.
2026-03-12 - Perf testing: under synthetic load (500 RPS) cache hit rate 88% with 10m TTL; P95 added latency 4ms. Ready for canary once Security sign-off complete.
